text:
Leah (Design): quick sync on paste/import behavior for the create-pool form. when users paste CSV rows we get 10+ validation errors and the page floods. want pattern recs: toast summary vs inline badges + error chips?
Omar (Eng): for paste flows, inline per-field errors kill scanability. prefer a compact toast summary that lists counts and a small inline error chip on the affected row + a "View details" panel. toast = low noise, panel = full context.
Priya (Eng): implementation note: the "View details" panel can anchor to the first invalid row and expand its fields. keep inline chips tappable to open panel. avoids huge page length.
Jia L: accessibility: toast summaries must be announced (`role=alert`) and the panel should receive focus when opened. inline chips need `aria-describedby` that references the panel content when expanded.
Noah (PM): what about error severity? some issues are warnings (duplicate name) vs blockers (missing required). maybe show red chips for blockers, amber for warnings, gray for info. chips should be actionable: click -> open row editor.
Leah (Design): love chips. microcopy debate: should chips say short reasons like "missing required" or more friendly "Please add a value"?
Priya (Eng): short and direct is better for bulk flows: "Missing value" / "Invalid format". we can add hover tooltips with longer guidance.
Jia L: SR note: include a longer explanation in the panel and ensure the chip has `aria-label="Missing value in row 3, open details"`. avoid relying on hover-only tooltips.
Omar (Eng): UX question: should we auto-collapse inline validation until user blurs the field? for paste flow we probably validate on paste and only show chips, not full inline errors until user opens details. keeps page stable.
Leah (Design): agree. validate on paste, show chips + summary. when user navigates back to a field, show inline error under that field. this way beginners still get field-level help.
Noah (PM): destructive confirmation inside the panel (e.g., "Remove row") pattern? typed-confirm too heavy for row deletion. modal with explicit copy + undo toast seems right.
Priya (Eng): technical: undo for row deletion should re-enqueue the row on client and call server patch with TTL. also ensure that undo is keyboard accessible and screen-reader friendly.
Jia L: modal accessibility: heading announced, body with consequences, focus trap, and primary button labeled fully like "Remove row from import". toast undo should have `role=alert` and keyboard focusable "Undo" link.
Leah (Design): required indicator conversation: asterisk vs explicit "Required" badge. in dense table/paste UX we should use small "Req" column header or an asterisk in column header tooltip that explains required columns. avoids per-cell clutter.
Omar (Eng): agree a column-level signal is much cleaner. columns can have a `*` in the header and header tooltip text "Required for pool creation". screen readers should include the header hint when focusing a cell.
Jia L: ensure header hints are included in the cell's accessible name via `aria-labelledby` so SR users know which columns are required.
Leah (Design): final microcopy bits: toast summary copy examples: "12 rows have errors 5 issues total7 — Open details" or shorter: "12 rows have errors — View". prefer concise.
Noah (PM): shorter is better for toast. full breakdown in the details panel.
Leah (Design): action items: - prototype paste flow with toast + chips + details panel - header-level required indicators + SR bindings - modal + undo pattern for row removal - accessibility checklist (role=alert, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, focus rules)
Priya (Eng): I'll review the prototype for focus behavior and undo TTL.
Omar (Eng): I'll wire the chips -> panel interactions.
Jia L: I'll run the accessibility checklist once the prototype is up.
Leah (Design): great, will drop a prototype link tomorrow. :sparkles:
